context: Hiroshi-elder shares stories about life in the Showa era with Sho-young.
purpose: Grandfather giving historical perspective to young grandchild.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: おじいちゃん、昭和って?
lines.style: Soft, wondering question. Leans in slightly, genuinely curious. Open throat, no rush. The tone of a child who expects a real answer from someone he trusts.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔の時代やな、若い頃の。
lines.en: Oh, that's the old time — when I was young.
lines.style: Warm, unhurried Kansai drawl. Eyes drift inward — not quite here, but not far away. A gentle settling into memory. Tone of someone who's been asked this before and doesn't mind being asked again.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: Was life really different back then?
lines.style: Soft, tentative. Searching for the shape of the answer before he hears it. Small voice — respectful of the oldness of the old days. Genuine wonder, not performance.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: おう、電話もない家、多かった。
lines.en: Yeah — lots of homes didn't even have phones.
lines.style: Matter-of-fact, almost fond about the strangeness of it. Slight Kansai roll on the affirmative. Slow unfold — giving him time to picture it. A small smile in the voice without overdoing it.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: Really? I can't even imagine that!
lines.style: Genuine astonishment. Bright, unburdened laugh underneath. No sarcasm — he truly cannot picture it. The exclamation lands with real wonder, not exaggeration.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 時代、ようけ変わったわ。
lines.en: Things have changed a lot in this time.
lines.style: Quiet philosophical weight. Not sad, not cheerful — observant. A Kansai lilt at the end. The tone of someone who has watched enough decades pass to know the shape of change.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: Tell me more! Tell me more stories!
lines.style: Bright, eager lean-forward energy. Open-throated desire — not demanding, but genuinely hungry to know. The kind of excitement that makes an old person want to keep talking.
